It differs from monolithic GPU voxel carving by overcoming VRAM limits through a stream-processing architecture, enabling the reconstruction of volumes significantly larger than the available video memory [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that the method differs from monolithic GPU voxel carving by overcoming VRAM limits through a stream-processing architecture, enabling the reconstruction of volumes significantly larger than the available video memory. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly supports this: it mentions that a single GPU kernel is limited to 256^3 voxels due to GPU memory constraints ('each GPU reconstruction kernel can use a maximum 256^3 voxels, since this is all that fits into the GPU memory'). It then introduces a 'scalable reconstruction scheme that exploit streaming computation' which divides the volume into 'small sub-volumes of a size that fits into the GPU memory.' It further details the process of sequentially transferring sub-volumes to and from GPU memory. Finally, it provides examples of large-scale reconstructions (e.g., 2,560 x 256 x 2,560 voxel grid) performed on hardware with only 512 MB video memory, confirming that the reconstructed volumes are significantly larger than the available video memory.
